name: Steroidogenesis Pathways, Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia, and MEN Syndromes

reference.source: Medical Biochemistry 5th ed / Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd ed
clinicalPearls: 21-Hydroxylase deficiency accounts for >90% of CAH, causing cortisol/aldosterone deficiency and androgen excess
Severe 21-hydroxylase deficiency presents in neonates with salt-wasting shock, hyperkalemia, and ambiguous genitalia in females
11-Beta-hydroxylase deficiency causes virilization with hypertension due to 11-deoxycorticosterone mineralocorticoid excess
MEN1 (menin mutation) features pituitary adenomas, parathyroid hyperplasia, and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors
MEN2 (RET proto-oncogene) features medullary thyroid carcinoma and phaeochromocytoma, requiring early thyroidectomy
reference.pathophysiology: Adrenal steroidogenesis converts cholesterol into mineralocorticoids, glucocorticoids, and sex steroids. Inactivating mutations in 21-hydroxylase abolish cortisol synthesis; absent negative feedback drives excessive pituitary ACTH secretion, hyperplastic adrenal cortical enlargement, and shunting of steroid precursors into androgen pathways. In MEN2, germline gain-of-function RET mutations induce constitutive receptor tyrosine kinase firing in neural crest-derived endocrine tissues.
additionalDifferentials: Multiple endocrine neoplasia Type 1 vs Type 2A/2B
additionalInvestigations: Serum 17-hydroxyprogesterone (17-OHP) baseline and post-ACTH stimulation test
Serum electrolytes: sodium, potassium, and plasma renin activity (salt-wasting state)
Genetic analysis of CYP21A2 gene for deletions and point mutations
RET proto-oncogene germline mutation testing and serum calcitonin for MEN2
